prompt: A particle of mass m travelling at speed u along the positive x-axis collides with a stationary particle of mass 2m. After the collision, the particle of mass m moves with speed v_1 at an angle of 60 degrees above the x-axis, and the particle of mass 2m moves with speed v_2 at an angle of 30 degrees below the x-axis. Which equation correctly expresses the conservation of momentum along the y-axis (perpendicular to the original motion)?
options: m v_1 sin(60 deg) - 2m v_2 sin(30 deg) = 0
m v_1 cos(60 deg) + 2m v_2 cos(30 deg) = mu
m v_1 sin(60 deg) + 2m v_2 sin(30 deg) = mu
m v_1 cos(60 deg) - 2m v_2 cos(30 deg) = 0

answer.explanation: Before the collision, the particles have zero velocity and zero momentum along the y-axis. Therefore, the total momentum along the y-axis after collision must be zero: m v_1 sin(60 deg) - 2m v_2 sin(30 deg) = 0.

distractor_explanations: Correct: initial y-momentum is zero, so the upward y-component of the first particle must equal the downward y-component of the second particle.
This expresses conservation of momentum along the x-axis, not the y-axis.
The initial y-momentum is zero, not mu; mu is the initial x-momentum.
Cosine represents the component along the x-axis, not the perpendicular y-axis.
hints: What was the total momentum along the y-axis before the collision?
Which trigonometric function gives the perpendicular component across the angle to the x-axis?
solution: Option 1 is correct. Initial y-momentum is zero, so p_1y + p_2y = 0 => m v_1 sin(60 deg) - 2m v_2 sin(30 deg) = 0.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Motion before collision is purely along the x-axis, so initial y-momentum p_y,initial = 0.
Step 2: Particle 1 scatters at 60 deg above x-axis: p_1y = + m v_1 sin(60 deg).
Step 3: Particle 2 scatters at 30 deg below x-axis: p_2y = - 2m v_2 sin(30 deg).
Step 4: Sum equals initial y-momentum: m v_1 sin(60 deg) - 2m v_2 sin(30 deg) = 0.
